prompts.prompt: Tell us your story. What unique opportunities or challenges have you experienced throughout your high school career that have shaped who you are today?
Describe a life event which you feel has prepared you to be successful in college.
In a few words, what are some of your life goals and objectives?
In a few words, why have you chosen your academic major(s)?
We know you have a lot of options. In a few words, why did you choose to apply to Texas A&M?
Briefly describe any educational plans you have beyond earning your bachelor’s degree.
Are there experiences or opportunities that have shaped or influenced your abilities or academic record, which you have not already written about?

intl_finance.document: Proof of finances (bank statement or equivalent liquid-funds document; third-party funds need a Declaration of Financial Support form or signed letter) submitted to International Student & Scholar Services (ISSS) to get the I-20. F-1 students must show at least one year of funding for the estimated cost of their program.
intl_finance.notes: Documents must be dated within 6 months of the date ISSS reviews them, on official letterhead, show the account holder name, current balance and currency (need not be USD, XE converter used), and be liquid assets; no Social Security numbers. Not accepted: statements of property/jewelry/cars, Chartered Accountant statements, pay stubs, trusts, passbooks. ISSS recommends bringing documents dated within 6 months to the visa interview. The ISSS page lists estimated cost-of-attendance tables for 2026 and 2027 I-20 requests; the dollar amounts were not read and are not copied here. The pages read do not give a calendar deadline for financial documents.

notes: The same questions appear on the international freshman page (source 2). The essay section does not carry a cycle label, but the page lists Fall 2027 entry dates (application opens Aug 1, College Station deadline Dec 1, additional documents Dec 15), so it is treated as 2026-27. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 100-word limit for the plans-beyond-bachelor's question is confirmed, not assumed: on both source 1 and source 2 it is the fourth item directly under the heading 'Required Short Answer Questions (100 words max):', before the next heading ('Optional Short Answer Question (250 words max)'). Applicants may use the Common App or ApplyTexas; ApplyTexas applicants also complete an Extracurricular Activities Form (not an essay). The College of Engineering's Entry to a Major (ETAM) essays are for students already enrolled, not part of the first-year application, so they are not included. The pages read do not state that financial documents are requested only after admission; ISSS says new F-1 students submit them to get an I-20, so timing is recorded as before_i20.
